newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Degussa aims double profit by 1998/99.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Degussa aims double profit by 1998/99.

text.p: German chemicals and metals group Degussa AG said on Tuesday it expects pre-tax profit in 1995/96 to be slightly above a record 404 million marks ($265 million) a year ago and hopes to double the figure to 800 million marks by 1998/99.
Chief executive Uwe-Ernst Bufe told his first news conference as Degussa chief that the company also expected sales to rise to 12 billion marks from 10.4 billion by 1998/99.

Degussa's business year ended on September 30 but Bufe said: "Some things can already be said today. In the final quarter of the 1995/96 financial year, the good profit situation continued as expected."
In 1994/95, pre-tax profit at Degussa jumped to 404 million marks from 280 million.
Bufe added that the earnings rise was needed to boost return on equity to 15 percent after tax.
The sales and profit forecasts were well received by the German stock market and Degussa shares ended bourse trade on Tuesday up 16 marks at 568.50 marks.

Bufe said Degussa was now divided into 11 operating business units, which are further divided into three segments -- chemical products, health and nutrition and precious metals and banking. The divisions are for reporting purposes and are not management divisions.
Breaking down the projected sales growth by sector, Bufe said that sales in its chemical products division would increase to 4.5 billion marks from 3.9 billion by 1998/99.

In the same period, its health and nutrition sector would register a sales increase to 3.5 billion marks from 2.8 billion, while sales in Degussa's precious metals and banking sector would grow to four billion marks from 3.7 billion.
Sales figures given are net of revenues from precious metals dealing.

Bufe nodded in the direction of a current German concern with providing shareholder value when he said that the group would also aim for slight increases in earnings per share (EPS) growth over coming years.
The consolidation of recent acquisitions could slightly hamper EPS growth in 1998/99 but growth was still anticipated. In 1994/95 EPS was 38 marks per share.
Degussa announced on Monday that it was planning to take over the remaining stake in the U.S. pharmaceuticals company Muro Pharmaceutical.

"Muro is a fast growing, very profitable pharmaceutical company. Its annual sales have quadrupled to 120 million marks between 1992 and today...and is working very successfully in research, production and marketing of proprietary products," said Bufe.

The group would finance the majority of the purchase with 630,000 Degussa shares, approximately 31.5 million marks in equity capital, for which Degussa's annual general meeting approved a capital increase of 40 million marks.
